definitions.explanation: A person who loves to eat and always wants to eat a lot. While it can mean glutton, it is often used affectionately or playfully, especially when referring to children or pets.

examples.japanese: うちの{犬|いぬ}は{食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}だ。
examples.english: Our dog is a big eater.

examples.japanese: {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}な{子供|こども}がおやつをねだっている。
examples.english: A greedy child is begging for snacks.

examples.japanese: {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}の{私|わたし}にとって、{旅行|りょこう}の{一番|いちばん}の{楽|たの}しみは{地元|じもと}の{料理|りょうり}を{食|た}べることだ。
examples.english: For a foodie like me, the best part of traveling is eating the local cuisine.

notes:
USAGE:
{食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう} has a playful, affectionate tone and is not strongly negative. It is commonly used for children and pets, or self-deprecatingly. The na-adjective form {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}な is also used as a modifier. The word {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}{万歳|ばんざい} was the title of a long-running TV cooking show.

SIMILAR WORDS:
{大食|おおぐ}い (big eater) and {食|た}べ{過|す}ぎ (overeating) focus on quantity, while {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう} emphasizes the love of eating itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}な{子|こ} (greedy child)
- {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}の{猫|ねこ} (greedy cat)
- {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}{万歳|ばんざい} (name of a famous TV show)
